notes:
## Changes since `v0.5.4`

### Features

- gather every split pane back into one group with Cmd+Option+\\ (Ctrl+Alt+\\ on Windows and Linux), beside the Cmd+\\ and Cmd+Shift+\\ split chords, as the Restore Single Group button does, whose tooltip now names the shortcut; with no split to undo the active tab flashes instead ([4df60887](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/4df60887752769c3fe6cf4eadd855f2e3858f6db))
- move the focus between split panes from the keyboard: Cmd+\[ / Cmd+\] step through them in reading order, as iTerm2, Ghostty and Warp do, and Cmd+Option+arrows go by direction, picking the neighbour sharing most of the edge, then the most recently used; Windows and Linux take Ctrl+Shift+\[ / \] and Ctrl+Alt+arrows since Ctrl+\[ is Escape there. SFTP back and forward keep Alt+arrows and give up Mod+\[ / \], and on macOS Ctrl+\[ and Ctrl+\] no longer fall back to the Cmd binding, so Escape and the telnet and virsh escape still reach the terminal ([d498ec9d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d498ec9de33da8dfe7956d9d9e3bd14ca0c99bae))
- make the ninth tab shortcut pick the last tab, as Chrome, Safari, Terminal and iTerm2 do, so the far end of a long tab bar is one key away; 1-8 still go by position ([4bbf7569](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/4bbf75690a91e62401e3227c8d1b3ba772c5dfbe))
- flash the active tab when a tab shortcut picks the tab already in sight, and shake the tab bar when it names no tab, since such a shortcut changed nothing on screen and looked as if it had not fired; reduced motion keeps a colour or opacity change instead ([b3dfa844](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b3dfa844b70efd517f0c4f3689eaded8890da3cb))
- switch to tabs 1-9 with Cmd+1-9 by default on macOS, since Terminal, iTerm2 and browsers use it there while Option+digit types symbols and is a readline count once Option acts as Meta; Windows and Linux keep Alt+1-9, and saved custom bindings are untouched ([d8ea9ad8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d8ea9ad8855207a1fa99fb5a150910606b7dd3b7))
- drag SFTP rows out onto a File Explorer or Finder folder (or the desktop) to download them there, since downloading always went through a folder picker: pressing a highlighted row, or a selected one in selection mode, starts a native drag; Windows drags empty placeholders named for each item and learns the folder from the shell's create notice, then deletes them, while macOS drags file promises and Finder names the folder; the download then runs as a normal batch with the conflict prompt and transfer list, window drops are ignored during the drag so placeholders are never uploaded, and a drop on anything but a folder says so; Linux does not offer it ([22468490](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/22468490e4716dacae781639ef07f028c41c037c))
- have zsh, fish and PowerShell report each command line (OSC 633 E) before its output starts, since tTerm rebuilt it from the keys and lost it when it came from history, Tab completion or a suggestion, leaving the tab unnamed: zsh and fish send it from preexec, PowerShell wraps PSReadLine's line editor once it has loaded and now sends C as well, backslashes and control characters go escaped as `\\\\` and `\\xHH`, and the frontend takes the reported line over a typed one and stops rebuilding lines once the shell reports them; bash and the copyable remote snippets still rely on the keys ([ef5f0aac](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/ef5f0aac95df5c02270ce17a5a17e836a4fa2314))
- show the unseen notification count on Linux docks, since Tauri sends it through libunity and only while the Unity desktop itself runs, so Ubuntu Dock, Dash to Panel, KDE Plasma's task manager and Plank never saw it: tTerm now sends the LauncherEntry Update signal over DBus itself for tTerm.desktop, hiding the count at zero, and keeps its session bus connection open since docks drop a count once its sender goes away; zbus was already built for the keyring, opener and single-instance plugins ([0906dee2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0906dee22e7d2e139861be91ec80ff8c63a15bbb))
- tell a Windows copy whose taskbar hides the notification count how to show it, since with Show badges on taskbar apps turned off the overlay never appears and nothing said why: Settings > Notifications now says so and points to Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors, read from the TaskbarBadges value that Windows leaves on when unset; the permission warnings now come from one table instead of a block each ([515a42aa](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/515a42aa413b64684e647f7ad3077d6a932d2521))
- put a red dot on the tray icon while system notifications wait unseen, since a window closed to the tray has no taskbar button and its count went out of sight: the dot sits in the icon's top right corner, cut out by a clear ring so it reads on light and dark trays, comes off once every notification is seen, and a tray icon added later starts with it ([da7ee08a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/da7ee08a9da50882ad59ef84106ca0599ec1478e))
- count unseen system notifications on the Windows taskbar button, since Windows ignored the app icon count and showed nothing: an app installed without a package identity has no badge there, so the frontend draws the count as a red disc (1 to 9, then 9+, sized to the display scale) and tTerm puts it on the taskbar button as an overlay, the way chat apps show theirs; the count now goes through set_unseen_notifications on every system, which keeps the overlay to put back when the window returns from the tray with a new taskbar button ([898b61fb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/898b61fb258b39beec6ac2c3117f2345ef2b6676))
- type the paths of files dropped on a local terminal at the prompt, since a drop there did nothing while the system terminals insert the path: each path is quoted for the tab's shell (backslashes for POSIX shells as macOS Terminal does, single quotes for PowerShell, double quotes for cmd as Windows Terminal does, /mnt/c paths for WSL and /c paths for Git Bash), and only the pane under the cursor takes it; SSH tabs still leave drops to the SFTP drawer ([98c58774](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/98c5877433cb11dd3e6e5a96c5a87302fa82acb8))
- count unseen system notifications on the app icon, since a notification missed while away left no trace outside the tab dots: each one tTerm raises while the window is in the background adds to the Dock badge (and Unity launchers on Linux), and seeing its tab, by clicking it, switching to it or coming back to a window that already shows it, takes its count off; Windows has no badge count and is left as it was ([117077ec](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/117077eceb3013d79a183cde1f95483bb846a78d))
- show each action's shortcut where the action is offered, since the keymap could only be discovered in Settings: tab and terminal context menu items show their chord on the right, and the new tab, command library, broadcast, SFTP, SFTP navigation and editor save buttons add it to their tooltips; labels come from the keymap in effect, so a rebound action shows its new chord and an unbound one shows none ([1ca86e78](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/1ca86e781e010a628bb97759c278e763f561d639))
- add a shortcut that renames the active tab, Mod+Shift+R by default, since renaming was only reachable through the tab's context menu: it opens the same rename dialog, can be rebound under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts > Tabs, and leaves the key alone on settings, tunnels and logs tabs, whose titles are fixed ([0b63ffe1](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0b63ffe1c21644b573e5b44c6c41168490104059))
- import ProxyCommand from SSH config files, since hosts that reach their server through one were imported without it and could not connect: a command that only hands the connection to an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy (nc -X, ncat --proxy, connect, corkscrew) becomes that proxy server, ssh -W %h:%p becomes a jump host as ProxyJump does, ProxyCommand none connects directly, and any other command is saved as a command proxy that asks before it first runs; proxies already in the list are reused, the command keeps its quotes for the shell, Host * sets it for the other hosts, and Key=Value lines are now read too ([89ee42de](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/89ee42de9b82ecfcd0a1bd30ba7ac98cf3052906))
- add the command kind to the proxy dialog and ask before a proxy command from elsewhere first runs, so ProxyCommand can be set up in Settings > Proxies: the dialog takes one command line with its tokens checked, hosts and the proxy list show a command as $ command, and an app-wide prompt shows the full command when a terminal, SFTP, tunnel or monitor connection needs one this device has not allowed yet, including prompts asked before the window was ready ([f4e1934e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f4e1934e8f342f5a28f5f34f83508f492f6d2e22))
- connect SSH sessions through a proxy command, OpenSSH's ProxyCommand, since hosts behind cloudflared, a bastion reached with ssh -W or other tunnels could not be reached through an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy: a command is a new kind in the proxy list, runs through the shell with the PATH of the login shell and with %h, %p, %r, %n and %% replaced, carries the first hop over its input and output, and reports its exit status and error output when it fails; since a command runs a program on this device, one that arrives through sync, a backup or an import runs only after the user allows it in a prompt, remembered on this device by the command's hash outside sync and backups ([8bd71034](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8bd71034cdceb8db1ad37ec8ccd9bccd4ecb60be))
- add a Proxies settings page to save proxy servers and choose this device's default, and a proxy choice in the host dialog, so the proxies the backend can dial can be set up and picked per host; deleting a proxy says how many hosts still connect through it ([606b3578](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/606b35781513bda188b9e38e012f5c761eae9f7e))
- connect SSH sessions through an HTTP CONNECT or SOCKS5 proxy, since networks that only let traffic out through a proxy, a company proxy or a local Clash or V2Ray, left hosts unreachable: proxy servers are saved in a list that syncs and backs up with profiles, each host connects through the device's default proxy, directly or through a chosen server, and the proxy carries the first hop of terminals, SFTP, tunnels, monitoring and connection tests, with errors that say whether the proxy, its password or the target failed ([a9023382](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/a9023382efbcd7968424f04d7dfa581a2b355d65))
- let a key's OpenSSH certificate be chosen per connection and per jump host, and import it from CertificateFile in ~/.ssh/config, since a certificate kept elsewhere than <key>-cert.pub could not be used, and explain a chosen certificate that is missing, expired or for another key before connecting ([769cd6ff](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/769cd6ff409aeb518a1937ccec997c8fa799d6a2))
- sign in with the OpenSSH certificate beside a key file, <key>-cert.pub, before the key alone, as ssh does, so hosts that trust a certificate authority instead of authorized_keys accept the key file, and skip a key file during automatic authentication only once the agent offered both its key and its certificate, so a renewed certificate on disk is still tried after an expired one in the agent ([529f614d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/529f614d79b72a2a378469ba47453f86f5ca6cf1))
- offer the OpenSSH certificates an SSH agent holds as certificates, since they were sent as the bare key inside, which a server that trusts only the certificate authority refuses, so Teleport, step ssh login and keys added with ssh-add beside a -cert.pub could not sign in through the agent ([f9f4ed41](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f9f4ed4175f4894db8e072a7017398d4b8546d2e))
- add a setting for the tab hover tooltip, off by default, since the tooltip with a tab's full title and connection popped up whenever the pointer crossed the tab bar; it covers both title-bar and split-group tabs and syncs with the other tab settings ([e5dfb085](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e5dfb085e29763c96a6cf720b9a877c58583d9a0))
- size the terminal log replay to its panel, with its own font size control and a Fit panel option on the toolbar, keeping the recorded columns and rows but never letting them overflow the panel, since the replay used a fixed font that left it small in a fullscreen window and the panel scrolled around xterm's own scrollback, and bring xterm's scrollbar up to date after each font change, since it only measures on resize or scroll and was left the wrong height and scrolled to the wrong line ([38952142](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/38952142a0be8244ba7f61fe289bf87caefc5b46))
- put new terminal logs in a folder per day by default, with the template {year}-{month}-{day}/{profile}-{host}-{time}-{sessionId}, so a busy log directory stays browsable, while settings already saved keep their own template ([12400b86](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/12400b8601d8bbef5ad5557d4b0bb65d68869b82))
- answer the XTGETTCAP query for Ms with the OSC 52 clipboard string over SSH, since neovim only copies through OSC 52 once the terminal reports it and every capability but Co was answered as unsupported ([f88560a2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f88560a2facb60d4cdce2182b1d5d61ce23ee391))
- select text with Option+drag on macOS while a program such as vim or tmux has the mouse, as iTerm2 does, since xterm.js only forces a selection there with macOptionClickForcesSelection and there was otherwise no way to select and copy ([05dfe58c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/05dfe58cf41d8647ba09867ea13e1fe6b7017f6a))
- let programs in the terminal copy to the clipboard with OSC 52, behind a terminal setting that is on by default and synced, so vim, neovim and tmux can copy over SSH, while clipboard queries are never answered so no program, local or remote, can read the clipboard ([d009b327](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d009b327428fc3d9c5fa87136949caf4198a2aa7))
- show the tab's own title after a running command's while another tab runs a command of the same title (claude · web, claude · api), since tabs running several agents at once all read claude and could not be told apart ([bf1c12ee](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bf1c12eebd7546c27bb631ee512afa0883791164))
- list this machine's default shell among the tab icon settings when the built-in list leaves it out, such as nu or xonsh, so its tabs' icon can be chosen there and not only tab by tab ([f6ba9352](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f6ba9352e6fe8d8299bf49135b1629960e3d9f68))
- let the shell icons on local tabs be turned off, and each shell's icon and color be picked from 67 icons and a palette in the appearance settings, with a tab's own icon set from its Edit Tab dialog, since the built-in icons and colors did not suit every theme or taste ([aece1e87](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/aece1e87019c71f940491e00792f7c4cc7b9cb34))
- show each local tab's shell as an icon before its title and set apart tabs in different directories of the same name with their parent directories (web/src, api/src), since tabs named after their directory no longer said which shell ran in them and could look the same ([f7476a5a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f7476a5a3d6d8fa857b396661add6c0b19e708b5))
- name local terminal tabs after their shell's working directory and show the command running in them, since tabs all called pwsh, pwsh-2, pwsh-3 told the user nothing about what each one was doing; a renamed tab keeps its name, the rename dialog can make it automatic again, and saved tabs with an old generated name switch over ([20534558](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/20534558c8b7eae5fe446175f5e5117e3e5ab5de))
- thank the open source projects tTerm is built on in a new About dialog, and list every third-party package that ships in the app with its license text under Open Source Licenses, collected at build time from cargo metadata for each release target and pnpm into public/licenses.json, since MIT, BSD, ISC and Apache ask that their notices travel with the binary ([29d8b79f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/29d8b79fef1c3a65825252bcda3a21c03449238c))

### Fixes

- leave Ctrl+\\ to the terminal on macOS instead of falling back to the Cmd+\\ split, since it sends SIGQUIT and an unbound Ctrl chord there otherwise borrows the Cmd binding ([3c7ac7d0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3c7ac7d0bf89f4178e6c8d866b9a1ba01167ff08))
- empty xterm's hidden textarea when a control key is sent, since xterm only empties it on Enter and Ctrl+C, so after Ctrl+J (a new line in Claude Code and Codex) the macOS Pinyin IME still read the committed Chinese as context and auto-spaced the next digit or letter, starting the new line with a stray space; arrow keys, Tab, Backspace and Escape left the same stale context, printable keys keep it, and a pending IME diff is left alone so no DEL is sent ([ded0d193](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/ded0d19364dc21f1d788bd05a78135f82cede367))
- switch to the Nth tab from the chord's digit instead of event.key, since Option+1 on macOS types "¡", so the shortcut matched by physical key but the handler read no digit and the tab never changed ([c6219b5f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c6219b5f1d36e0966f567c3eb80a28718e8b41e0))
- stop naming a tab after a line typed into the agent it runs, since a command line recalled with Up or completed with Tab could not be rebuilt from the keys, so the first line typed into the agent's prompt became the running command instead: lines typed while command marks show a command running (or a full-screen program) no longer count as commands or go into the history, a typed line no longer names a command that already started, and on PowerShell and cmd Enter at the prompt now starts the command after the typed line is noted, including the first command of a new tab, which used to wait for a D mark ([5ffd758e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5ffd758e3758b0ef007b9e8c3d1ea13f2c6d713d))
- count a system notification on the app icon only once it is shown, since one the system refused or that failed still added to the badge: a notification whose tab came into sight while it was on its way is not counted either ([c023cfd7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c023cfd7a2b77ed4904d596be250439e4c64a1bc))
- tell a copy whose app icon badge is off how to turn it on, since macOS asks for badges only once and a copy that allowed notifications before tTerm asked for badges kept the Dock count hidden with no sign why: Settings > Notifications now says so and points to Badge app icon under System Settings > Notifications > tTerm ([9b5c8e57](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9b5c8e57ca7aaa0e72c77430b8d4d27704db31e0))
- show the Dock badge on macOS, since the Dock hides an app's badge unless its notification authorization includes badges and tTerm asked only for alerts and sounds: the request now asks for badges too; a copy that was already authorized may need Badge app icon turned on under System Settings > Notifications ([619c8cb8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/619c8cb8482c6b70e2d27927192383b2c64859ce))
- show Codex, OpenCode or pi at work again as soon as their wait is answered, since Codex runs no hook between the approval and the end of the approved tool, which left the tab paused for as long as the command ran: typing in the waiting terminal now resumes the spinner, and a refusal is put right by the agent's own report, which Claude Code does not send, so its waits are left as they were ([5864ca10](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5864ca107f637679eb7c8de9bc921b29183783c0))
- keep the tab's spinner while Codex, OpenCode or pi works on after Esc or Ctrl+C, since Codex's Esc closes a popup first and its Ctrl+C clears a draft without stopping anything, which cleared the spinner for the rest of the turn: these agents report a real stop themselves, so only Claude Code's is still guessed from the keys ([2a165f78](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2a165f78ba3436e704e2e4418baf2a1c399b23a0))
- tell the PTY the new size once the terminal font finishes loading, since the cell size changes the column count without resizing the pane, so the shell stayed at the fallback font's width ([2013c9e9](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2013c9e9d68b659aaaad6a10e9288c8e7a95e220))
- open the SSH PTY at the newest size the terminal reported while connecting, since resizes queued during connection and authentication reached the shell only as it printed its first prompt, and an older bash then redrew the prompt over the line above and left a broken copy behind ([598e8e61](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/598e8e613d289e9fa78c9ed0452758b93358af29))
- keep a terminal log readable when quitting cuts its compression short, by writing the archive under a .partial name and renaming it once complete, removing unfinished and duplicate archives the first time the log directory is maintained, and reading a part from its plain file when both copies are left, since a truncated .gz beside its log used to duplicate the text or make the whole session fail to open, and the part was never compressed again ([70a65711](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/70a6571167af1b96a012b46b3727c6a7f337aca1))
- stop marking a background tab for output written to the alternate screen, checked once the chunk is parsed, since full-screen programs like Codex redraw in answer to focus and mouse reports and kept the activity dot coming back every time the user left the tab, while a program leaving the alternate screen on exit still marks it ([993b5986](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/993b5986fc7ea7015413824c59d6176b6da0dc46))
- close a tab's tooltip when the pointer leaves it through the close button, by dropping the close button's stopPropagation on mouseleave that kept the tab from ever seeing its own, and close any open tooltip once the pointer is over something else, leaves the window, presses or the window blurs, since a missed mouseleave left the tooltip stuck until its tab was clicked ([e8cda467](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e8cda467c52fd7bcc7d263d6da641c9f7df2bd26))
- play the notification sound on Linux when it is asked for, through notify-send's sound-name hint, since the request's sound flag was ignored there and Rust 1.99 flags it as never read ([79bbc97a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/79bbc97a35a9fe15535c3505872fe0a2fb91fbe2))
- write Codex's Windows hook command without quotes, since Codex hands it to cmd /C as one Rust-quoted argument where each quote arrives as \\" and cmd failed every hook looking for a program named \\"C:\\...; a path with spaces goes in by its short name ([77fddf23](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/77fddf232a7494d1aa62e46e58190f1fb927c6bf))
- send a reattached session's output to the page that created it again, since a reloaded page restores its tabs with the same session, which kept writing to the old page's channel and left the tab blank and deaf to typing ([5b1e09da](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5b1e09da865b422615cd950aaec6f777dd4a7c98))
- report Codex's work, waits and finished turns from Windows too: its hooks run through cmd /C with a hidden console, where the POSIX hook finds neither ps nor a terminal and fails, so the hooks also get a commandWindows that runs tTerm itself (--agent-report), which attaches to the console of the first ancestor with a window (Codex's tab) and writes the report there, or with the session's id to every Codex console when Codex runs in a background server ([e86d8fa1](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e86d8fa13516ec5725f223ae2ce2de89159cb2ad))
- show tooltips below their trigger when they do not fit above it, and give workspace tab headers the tab tooltip too, since a tab's tooltip in the title bar opened above the window and never showed ([9bf2d0f2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9bf2d0f2c9ae9a863f75f75ae5eff2a46aae7482))
- send typed and pasted input to an SSH session through the same input thread as a local shell, so a paste is paced by the remote output and Ctrl+C drops the rest of it, since a paste went into the SSH channel whole and a Ctrl+C typed after it reached the remote only once all of it had been sent ([0e6d2e21](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0e6d2e2188dbbfb403d72abd10731f04a8e00c90))
- write typed and pasted input to a local shell on a thread of its own, feed a paste only as fast as the shell answers it with output, and let Ctrl+C drop the rest of it and empty the Windows console's input buffer, since write_pty wrote the whole paste on the main thread and froze the window while the PTY was full, and a console shell then took all of it at once, showed nothing for seconds and worked through it past any Ctrl+C ([a2961fda](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/a2961fda83b6520175b21a809937b2f9c51517df))
- give the keyboard focus back to the terminal after renaming a tab, choosing from a context menu, closing a dialog, the tab search, broadcast or transfer panel, or the SFTP drawer, and keep clicks on tabs and toolbar buttons from taking it, since a dialog read where the focus came from only after its autoFocus input had taken it and so restored nothing, and a closing menu or panel dropped the focus on the page body, leaving typing to go nowhere until the terminal was clicked ([c4db70c1](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c4db70c19b3d97a4a3e998523bf8c821e79d35e3))

### Performance

- write each session's terminal log on its own thread with buffered output, so logging never waits on the disk on the SSH task, the PTY reader or the main thread where keyboard input arrives, dropping output and noting a log_gap event only when 16 MiB is already queued, flushing at least once a second and fsyncing only on rotation or close, measuring disk usage in the background instead of walking the log directory on every status request, checking the size limit as logs grow, and waiting up to 3 seconds on quit for logs to write out ([e7b7dd83](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e7b7dd8323dab2f86da7266f84ecab8112a7fcbd))
- run the commands that read the database, the keychain or config files on a worker thread through run_blocking, since as synchronous commands they ran on the main thread and froze the window while they waited ([297d0e67](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/297d0e67ee71bdd76cc70864990e2b6c33a880bd))
- throttle SFTP transfer progress by time in the backend, at most one report per 100 ms per transfer with the final one always sent, and lower the drawer's own throttle to 50 ms so delivery jitter drops none, since the 64 KB byte gate was smaller than one 255 KB step and a fast transfer sent about 400 events a second that the drawer threw away all but ten of ([929bfd01](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/929bfd01e3bcf7b15e5846d20fc79136724300cd))
- pause the server monitor while its tab is out of view and keep its connection open meanwhile, and connect a tab restored in the background only once it is shown, since every SSH tab ran the metrics script on its server every few seconds whether or not anyone could see the result ([9b4fb78a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9b4fb78a1093b3b2b2844b869681f04672b98f4f))
- load the SFTP file icon manifest when the drawer opens instead of with the app, showing the plain folder and file icons until it arrives, since vscode-material-icons put about 256 kB into the main bundle for a drawer most sessions never open ([680d1b90](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/680d1b901592f31b04a97501dc56fe74e9a73cee))
- create a terminal session, list and delete backup history, and preview and import SSH config off the main thread, and load the macOS login shell environment in the background at startup, since create_pty read saved passwords, waited for the session map and started the shell on the main thread, and the first local tab on macOS froze the window while $SHELL -l ran ([86861217](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/86861217614be23709aa60278122c35677d13f1e))
